textbookText: The bimetallic thermostat is a device made up of two thin metallic strips of different linear expansivities welded together along their lengths. Brass - steel bimetallic strips are the examples of bimetallic thermostat. When brass-steel thermostat is heated, the brass having greater value of linear expansivity expands more than the steel. Since the two strips are welded together, the thermostat bends into an arc with brass in greater curvature. As a result, electric contact breaks as in figure 10.11(b). This special design can be used as safety measure to control the overflow of heat in many electrical appliances, and hence to save from accidents.

In the above example, the thermostat bends into an arc with brass in greater curvature due to their difference in thermal expansion. This difference in expansions of two bodies, having different values of coefficient of thermal expansion, when they are heated through the same range of temperature is called differential expansion. The principle of differential expansion is used in many appliances like electric irons, rice cookers, electric heating systems, aquarium, etc. as thermo switches for automatic switching of electric supply.
